angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 253,235 km at 27.31 pc = 0.12 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 36.6105 +/- 0.0243 mas (same row, RUWE 1.30): 27.31 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.364 +/- 0.012 solar radii from Kemmer et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of GJ 3473 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...642A.236K/abstract): 253,235 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.36 +/- 0.016 solar masses from Kemmer et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of GJ 3473 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...642A.236K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3347 +/- 54 K from Kemmer et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 3473 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...642A.236K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Kemmer et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 3473 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...642A.236K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gj-3473.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.872, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
